bull.b: Rapid DTC growth strengthens control over pricing, customer relationships, and brand presentation while improving sales mix. A larger owned-channel base can support durable margin quality and reduce reliance on third-party retailers as On expands internationally.

Strong gross and net margins, combined with substantial free cash flow, indicate that On is converting growth into meaningful earnings and internally generated funding. This supports continued product investment, retail expansion, and financial resilience as the business scales.

A broader product and sport-category portfolio can increase addressable demand and reduce dependence on a single running franchise. The multi-year strategy also shows ambition to preserve premium margins while scaling the brand across additional consumer use cases.

bear.b: Slower wholesale growth, particularly in the Americas, indicates that some retail partners are seeing weaker sell-through in a promotional marketplace. Persistent channel softness could moderate revenue growth and make inventory and product-launch execution more important.

A materially higher inventory balance increases the importance of disciplined sell-through and assortment management, especially while wholesale shipments are being calibrated. If demand or channel timing disappoints, excess stock could pressure margins or working-capital efficiency.

Higher import tariffs create an external cost pressure that can weigh on gross margin or require pricing and sourcing responses. Because potential refunds depend on timing and were excluded from guidance, near-term profitability and cash benefits remain uncertain.
